From ISAIF, para 191:

"One should think twice before encouraging any other social conflict than that
between the power-holding elite (which wields technology) and the general
public (over which technology exerts its power). For one thing, other conflicts
tend to distract attention from the important conflicts (between power-elite
and ordinary people, between technology and nature); for another thing, other
conflicts may actually tend to encourage
 technologization, because each side in such a conflict wants to use
technological power to gain advantages over its adversary."

The Democrats seem to be trying to bring up the issue of the rich and powerful
vs. ordinary people (aka the middle class and the poor), but this seems limited
to a debate on the tax cut plans proposed by Bush and Gore. The Dems, along
with the Repubs, seem otherwise to be caught up in a number of the regular vote
getting election issues, including many the electorate seem sick of.

The Greens seem to be taking the bull by the horns, see 

http://www.votenader.com/ 

However, in another section, FC says not to vote Green, because he thinks that
things need to get to a crisis stage before they can get better. I don't think
that's really necessary anymore, though I don't know how TK feels about it this
year. Fewer and fewer people are bothering to vote, and corporations are just
getting more powerful.

As far as TK's voting rights, I wonder if he has ever voted? Just as a
curiosity.

I heard something on "Morning Edition" on NPR recently about inmates in
Massachussetts who may be casting their last ballot, as there is a referendum
in MA about taking away the right to vote for convicted felons in prison in
that state. I think that there are about four states that allow prisoners to
vote, if they reside in a prison in that state.

A final thought - your vote represents your opinion. The media has us thinking
that it's a football pool, where you have to bet your vote on a winner. It's
the ultimate BS. Think about what's truly important to you, check out the
candidates and then make your decision.

-IB
